LESSON: HISTORICAL DEVELOPMENT OF AGRICULTURE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa
Topic 4.2: Historical Development of Agriculture
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Historical Development of Agriculture, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa in Grade 7 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why did people start practising agriculture in Africa? 2. How did Agriculture begin in Africa?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Historical Development of Agriculture together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: learners carry out research on the factors that favoured growing of crops and rearing of animals in

selected regions during early agriculture,(in Egypt, Nubia, and in the Rift Valley of the Eastern African region and report

the findings to the class,

● Communication and collaboration: Learners apply listening and speaking skills as they compose poems the importance of

domestication of plants and animals in Africa.

Values:
Patriotism: learners develop citizenship as they discuss the contribution of the Nile Valley agriculture to world civilisation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Social Cohesion: learners discuss the contribution of the Nile Valley agriculture to the world civilisation,

Link to other Subjects:

● Learners use knowledge of animal husbandry as they research on animals kept and types of crops which were grown during

early agriculture in Egypt, Nubia and in Rift valley of the Eastern African region.
